latin: Quod dicunt Cabalistae, beatificandos nos in speculo lucente reposito sanctis in futuro saeculo, idem est praecise, sequendo fundamenta eorum, cum eo quod nos dicimus, beatificandos sanctos in filio.
translation: What the Cabalists say -- that we are to be beatified in the shining mirror laid up for the saints in the age to come -- is, following their own foundations, precisely the same as what we say: that the saints are to be beatified in the Son.
translation_note: 'speculo lucente' (the shining mirror) is glossed as the sixth sefirah, which Pico regularly calls 'the great Adam' and treats as one of his standard symbols for Christ (paraphrase; farmer1998:27560).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch20, from Latin at farmer1998:27529
attribution: Pico's own opinion (section 11>, Cabalistic conclusions confirming the Christian religion by his own opinion) (farmer1998:27529).
doctrine: Farmer's note explains that the Cabalists' 'shining mirror' and the Christian claim that the saints are beatified in the Son come to the same thing, following the Cabalists' own foundations, because the 'shining mirror' is the sixth sefirah, which Pico regularly identifies with 'the great Adam,' one of his standard symbols for Christ (paraphrase; farmer1998:27560). The thesis is thus an instance of Pico's programme of showing Kabbalah and Christian doctrine to coincide (farmer1998:27529).
historiography: A German study of Pico's Kabbalistic epistemology quotes the thesis's Latin in full at page 542, in a discussion it locates under the Christological interpretation of the sefirah Tiferet, alongside thesis 11>51 and a reference to Archangelus's Interpretationes in dogmata (kabbalah_paradigma:1888, 1889); the study's own argument, given in German, is not established here beyond this bibliographic placement.
not_established: The kabbalah_paradigma study's discursive argument about the thesis, beyond the Latin quotation and its placement under the Christological reading of Tiferet, is not established here, the German text not having been translated (kabbalah_paradigma:1888).
